content: - We propose a UAV-enabled MEC system tailored for complex urban terrains. In this system, a UAV departs from an initial position and flies to a final destination, providing offloading services to nearby UDs. To accurately estimate the signal strength, we design a terrain-aware channel model. Unlike existing blockage-aware channel models that assume simple terrains with flat topographies, our proposed model can identify blockages caused by complex terrains. This capability makes it applicable to a wider range of urban environments, offering greater flexibility and broader applicability.

- We study a CMOP by jointly optimizing UAV flight trajectory, destination, and resource allocation. This joint optimization ensures reduced task completion time while enhancing safety on complex urban terrains.

- We propose a multi-tasking CMOEA with a task-adaptive mechanism. This mechanism can retain historically effective genetic operators and adaptively assigns different genetic operators to individuals based on their specific tasks during the evolution process, thereby enhancing the search capability and convergence performance of the proposed algorithm. Numerical results demonstrate that our algorithm significantly outperforms baseline algorithms in terms of solution diversity and convergence.
